Extract audio clips for BirdNET detections

Source: R/birdnet_extract_clips.R
birdnet_extract_clips.Rd

Cuts a short audio clip for each detection in a BirdNET output table and saves all clips in one folder, for example to validate detections without needing the original recordings. Each clip runs from the start of the detection to its end, plus a buffer before and after.

Usage

birdnet_extract_clips(
  data,
  output_dir,
  audio_dir = NULL,
  buffer = 3,
  file = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing BirdNET output, with columns for the file path, start time, end time, species common name, and confidence (detected automatically).

output_dir

Character. Folder where the clips are saved. It is created if it does not exist.

audio_dir

Character or NULL. Folder containing the original audio recordings, searched including subfolders. Only used for files that are not found at the path stored in data. Defaults to NULL, which uses the stored paths only.

buffer

Numeric. Seconds added before the start and after the end of each detection. Defaults to 3.

file

Character or NULL. Where to save the table as a CSV file (must end in .csv). Defaults to NULL, which saves it as detections_clips.csv in output_dir, next to the clips.

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE, the function stops before extracting anything when the table file already exists, so that a table you have already validated is not replaced by accident. Defaults to FALSE.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses the status messages about how many clips were extracted or could not be created. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

The input data frame with additional columns:

clip_file

The name of the clip file in output_dir, or NA if the clip could not be created.

clip_start

Start of the clip in the original recording, in seconds.

clip_end

End of the clip in the original recording, in seconds.

Details

The detection table, with the clip columns added (see Value), is saved as a CSV file in the same folder, so the folder holds everything needed to validate the detections.

File names. Clips are saved in the same audio format as the original recording (e.g. WAV stays WAV, MP3 stays MP3) and are named <ID>_<recording name>_<start>_<end>_<species common name>_<confidence>.<extension>, where:

  • ID is the row number of the detection in data, with leading zeros (01, 02, ...), so the clips sort in the same order as the table.

  • start and end are the detection times in seconds (without the buffer).

  • the species common name has characters that are unsafe in file names replaced with _.

  • confidence is the detection confidence, rounded to three decimals.

For example, 01_20230518_133500_12_15_Barred_Owl_0.873.wav. Because every name starts with its own ID, names are always unique.

Finding the audio. For each detection, the function first uses the file path stored in the table. If that file no longer exists (for example because the recordings were moved to another drive), it looks for a file with the same name inside audio_dir, including all subfolders. If several files have that name, the one whose parent folders best match the original path is used.

Clips near the edges. A clip is trimmed to fit inside the recording, so a detection near the start or end of a file gets a shorter buffer on that side. The times actually used are returned in clip_start and clip_end.

See also

birdnet_subsample(), birdnet_launch_validation()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sampled <- birdnet_subsample(my_data, n = 100, seed = 1)

clips <- birdnet_extract_clips(
  sampled,
  output_dir = "validation_audio",
  audio_dir = "path/to/recordings",
  buffer = 3
)
# "validation_audio" now holds the clips and detections_clips.csv
} # }
